title: Scheduled multiformat customer deliveries with priority fences and format-fallback
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Several enterprise customers require day/week scheduled deliveries of their usage and billing records with both S3 and webhook delivery options. Current pipeline supports ad-hoc CSV and S3 delivery but does not gracefully handle: per-tenant delivery priority, failures that require format fallback (e.g., when CSV generation causes OOM for very wide schemas), partial/resumable shard delivery, or prioritized quarantine to prevent noisy tenants from impacting the global export throughput.

This ticket will design and implement: a scheduling layer that enforces tenant-level priority fences, a composite manifest that describes shards and format candidates, a format-fallback mechanism (CSV -> newline-delimited JSON -> compressed columnar shard) when primary generation fails or would exceed resource budgets, resumable delivery semantics for webhooks and S3 multipart uploads, and observability/telemetry to track per-tenant SLA for deliveries. The goal is to provide predictable latency for high-priority customers while preserving lower-priority fanout with graceful degradation and strict auditability.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduled export jobs can be configured per-customer with priority (high/medium/low) and a delivery window (cron-like).
Scheduler enforces priority fences so no more than X concurrent high-priority deliveries run across the cluster (configurable).
Composite manifest is generated per-export describing shards, formats attempted, checksums, and delivery targets, and is stored with the export object.

Format-fallback policy is implemented: if CSV generation fails or estimated memory > configured threshold, system retries with compact NDJSON; if NDJSON also fails for resource reasons, fall back to compressed Parquet/columnar shard and mark in manifest.
S3 deliveries support resumable multipart uploads and atomic manifest/marker object to signal completion.
Webhook deliveries support HMAC-signed payloads, exponential backoff with jitter, per-tenant rate limits, and manual quarantine toggles.
Export delivery is idempotent: replays for the same manifest/shard do not result in duplicate billing events or duplicated files (checksums and object idempotency keys validated).

Observability: dashboards show per-tenant export success rate, average time-to-delivery, format-fallback rate, and the current active priority fences. Alerts fire if high-priority SLA misses exceed 1%.
End-to-end tests and a staging rollout prove a simulated noisy tenant cannot push high-priority customers beyond their SLOs.
technical_notes: Scheduler: extend the existing export scheduler to include a per-tenant 'priority_score' and an eviction/fence subsystem. Enforce global tokens for high priority to limit concurrency. Consider soft vs hard fences.

Manifest: JSON manifest schema v2 (flat key-value map) with fields: export_id, tenant_id, scheduled_time, shards: [shard_id, row_count, estimated_size_bytes, format_attempts], delivery_targets, completion_marker, checksums. Manifest stored in export-store (S3 + DB pointer).

Format generation: implement streaming CSV and NDJSON writers with memory windows. Introduce 'estimate_step' that computes cardinality/row-width heuristics to decide fallback before full materialization. For heavy rows, stream to columnar writer (Parquet) using chunked buffer. Ensure writers produce deterministic checksums.

Delivery: S3 -> use multipart uploads with server-side encryption (SSE-KMS) by default for enterprise customers. On success, write a completion marker object like _complete.json with manifest ref. Webhooks -> deliver signed POST with X-Export-Signature (HMAC-SHA256). Support mutual TLS for selected customers.
Idempotency: add export_run_id + shard_index as idempotency key. Backend will skip duplicate writes for same key within retention window. Database upserts are used for manifest state transitions.

Backpressure: implement token-bucket per-tenant and shard-level concurrency semaphore; noisy tenant detection that moves tenant into a 'quarantine' state where deliveries are delayed and admins notified.
Permissions/Audit: every manifest change must be recorded in audit logs (actor, timestamp, change). Integrate with KMS for envelope encryption keys.

Observability: new tracing spans across scheduler -> generator -> delivery. Emit metrics: export.manifest.created, export.shard.generated, export.delivery.attempt, export.delivery.success, export.fallback.rate. Tag metrics with tenant_id, priority, format.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (prototype): implement manifest v2 and streaming NDJSON writer behind feature flag. Run synthetic jobs in staging for 72h and validate memory and timing.
Phase 1 (canary): route 5% of scheduled jobs (non-enterprise tenants) through scheduler with priority fence enforcement. Monitor SLOs and fallback rate.
Phase 2 (enterprise opt-in): enable multipart S3 + HMAC webhooks for a subset of enterprise customers with dedicated tokens. Observe idempotency behavior.
Phase 3 (full rollout): enable priority fences by default, allow customers to set priority via Console, and remove feature flag after 2 weeks with no regressions.
testing_plan: Unit tests for CSV/NDJSON/Parquet writers including deterministic checksum tests and simulated OOM paths.
Integration tests for manifest lifecycle, resumable multipart uploads, and webhook retry logic (with a local webhook sink and chaos injection).

Performance tests to validate that a noisy tenant with 10x normal row width cannot reduce throughput for high-priority tenants below configured SLOs. Use k6 load harness and recorded production row-width distributions.
Security tests: verify HMAC signing, signature rotation, and optional mTLS handshake for webhooks; ensure KMS keys rotate without breaking existing manifests.
notes_and_risks: Risk: Incorrect heuristics may lead to unnecessary fallback and higher storage costs. Mitigation: conservative thresholds and telemetry to tune heuristics post-launch.
Risk: Multipart upload edge cases (aborted parts) could leave orphan objects. Mitigation: background reaper job to clean stale parts and strict completion marker semantics.
Risk: Quarantine semantics could delay important data for compliance customers. Mitigation: admin override and SLA-tiered quarantine rules.
Operational cost: format-fallback to Parquet may increase compute for conversion; include cost tagging on exported manifests for chargeback.
dependencies_notes: Relies on ENG-34021 for manifest pagination/resumable-download primitives and ENG-42109 for webhook retry/backoff framework.
Coordination required with customer-success for communicating new priority field and with Console PM to expose scheduling UI.
comments: 2026-02-13 - Asha Patel: Initial draft. Reached out to PM (Sofia Martinez) for product acceptance criteria and to Security for webhook HMAC requirements.

2026-02-20 - Liam O'Connor: Prototype NDJSON writer and estimator done. Found CSV writer can OOM when row width > 8MB due to internal buffer; updated design to stream and estimate before materializing row. Refer to PR: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4921 (draft).

2026-02-27 - Sofia Martinez (PM): Product request - add tenant-level 'priority' exposed in Console and API and ensure we support retroactive re-run of exports from Console. Added to acceptance criteria.
2026-03-02 - Security (Tamar Lee): Reviewed webhook plan. HMAC is required, mTLS optional. Need key rotation plan documented and secrets stored in Vault. Marked security_review_required.

2026-03-05 - Infra (Jamal Nguyen): Raised concern about storage cost if many fallbacks to Parquet. Recommend adding a retention and compacting job to convert transient Parquet to cheaper cold storage after 7 days. Added to notes.

2026-03-09 - Liam O'Connor: Created staging harness and smoke tests. Observed fallback rate of 0.7% on recorded production workloads. Memory profile looks acceptable with current thresholds. Scheduling fence token default values proposed: high=8, medium=25, low=100.
